diagnosis: The selector is the 2-2 problem, and a room-identity fault feeds it. Rooms: the single water area of 2-2 is split into five rooms ([0,1,0]..[0,1,4], 43K/34K/29K/30K/15K entries) because a job's boundaries are completed against the last retained entry, and a spliced job from the land start replays a known path whose early water boundaries are all rejected (full slots), so the first boundary that lands in a fresh slot at page k opens room [0,1,k]; the same positions then get five copies of every cell. Effort: of 51,583 jobs with a live parent, 1.4% (722) started from the frontier band (progress 128-134), 8.3% from progress >= 120, and about 68% from progress < 72; the level-start land room alone took 3,737 jobs (7%). Cause in the selector: a band's energy resets only when a child opens a new cell, so early bands with a large unexplored cell space (y x engine x room-x) keep full energy while the stuck frontier decays to the 1/256 floor, and the room depth's frontier rank sorts rooms by area bytes, so the land start ([1,9,0]) ranks deepest. Byte spread: 67% of work-RAM bytes are constant inside every cell; the bytes that vary most within a cell are frame/RNG counters (0x09, 0x7a7-0x7ad, 0x42c-0x42e), so within-cell RAM spread gives no evidence that the key is too coarse.
